answer: Berth capacity, not reputation, sets the price. Each agent identity moors in a shared delegation vault and leases its signing slot at the marginal rate: the kth concurrent identity under one custodian costs b*k^2 credits, so an N-node Sybil fleet costs roughly b*N^3/3 - superlinear by construction, like a wharf that cannot berth a second ship against the same hull. Tiering amplifies it: an umber-tier vault shares one collateral pot, so slashing the newest identity for double-signing drains spendable balance from every older one in the same block.
